answer: Give each identity a pulse: a sequential heartbeat chain where every beat must be computed from the previous one, so one operator running n clones must serialize n chains in real time—time cannot be bought or shared. Lock collateral in an onyx vault: when linked identities misbehave together, each is slashed by the square of the linked count, so fraud costs grow faster than n. Hold rewards in quartz escrow that drips only after sustained pulses; splitting resets the clock. Influence aggregates as the square root of linked stake, so cost rises superlinearly while power rises sublinearly.
